Histamine H2 Receptor Antagonists: Mechanism of Action, Therapeutic Uses and Adverse Effects

Mechanism of Action

  • H2 receptor antagonists work by suppressing gastric acid secretion by competitively antagonizing the histamine H2 receptors located on gastric parietal cells

H2 Blockers

  • FDA approved H2 blockers include:
  • Cimetidine
  • Famotidine
  • Nizatidine

Therapeutic uses

  • H2 blockers are FDA approved for:
  • Short term treatment of uncomplicated GERD
  • Gastric and duodenal ulcers (PPI is first line)
  • Mild to infrequent heartburn or indigestion
  • Off label uses include:
  • Stress ulcer prophylaxis (e.g. in trauma and burn patients) (PPI is first line)
  • Esophagitis and gastritis treatment (PPI is first line)
  • In GI hemorrhage treatment (PPI is first line)
  • Urticaria
  • H. Pylori eradication therapy (PPI is first line)
  • Heartburn during pregnancy (Antacids are first line)

Pharmacokinetics

  • H2 blockers are available as oral fromulations and they have good absorption after oral administration
  • Onset of action start in about an hour after administration and duration of action is from 4- 10 hours
  • All of them have the same efficacy in decreasing gastric acid secretion

Adverse effects

  • H2 Blockers are generally well tolerated
  • Adverse effects include:
  • Hypotension
  • Headache
  • Drowsiness
  • Fatigue
  • Abdominal pain
  • Constipation or diarrhea
  • Cimetidine and famotidine may lead to CNS side effects in patients older than 50, those include:
  • Delirium
  • Confusion
  • Hallucination
  • Slurred speech
  • Prolonged and high doses of cimetidine are linked with development of gynecomastia, reduced sperm count and impotence in men; galactorrhea in women; this is solved with drug discontinuation
  • Tolerance and tachyphylaxis occur within 7 to 14 days of continued treatment
  • That is why intermittent or as needed use is preferred for these medications
  • Small bowel bacterial overgrowth or C. difficile infection can occur with these medications but it is rare

Drug interactions

  • Cimetidine is a potent CYP P450 enzyme inhibitor, it raises the levels of medications that are metabolized by CYP, e.g. theophylline, SSRI and warfarin
